title: Jesus Christ: The Final Revelation
speaker: Pastor Stephen Thomas

outline.title: The Context of the Epistle
subpoints: Written to Jewish Christians tempted to return to Judaism
Theme: The supremacy and sufficiency of Christ

outline.title: Christ as the Final Revelation
subpoints: God spoke in various ways through prophets in the past
God has spoken finally through His Son in these last days
Christ is the culmination and goal of all Old Testament revelation

outline.title: The Sufficiency of Christ
subpoints: Christ is the 'better' than angels, Moses, and the priesthood
Seeing Christ is seeing the Father

outline.title: Application: Rejecting Pluralism
subpoints: Christ is the only way and the ultimate truth
Do not seek revelation beyond or behind Christ

summary:
This sermon, the first in a series on the book of Hebrews, focuses on verses 1 and 2 to establish the supremacy and sufficiency of Jesus Christ. The author of Hebrews wrote to Jewish Christians who were considering abandoning their faith in Christ to return to the Mosaic Law. The central argument is that God’s revelation is not a series of equal options but a progression that culminates in Christ. While God spoke in various ways through the prophets in the past, He has now spoken finally and fully through His Son. Christ is not merely a greater revelation but the final word of God, rendering all previous forms of revelation as shadows pointing to the substance found in Him.

The message emphasizes that there is no progression beyond Christ. As F.F. Bruce noted, the story of divine revelation moves up to Christ but never away from Him. To seek truth or spiritual fullness outside of or beyond Christ is to reject the finality of God’s word. The sermon highlights that Christ is the 'better' than angels, Moses, and the old covenant priesthood, and that seeing Christ is equivalent to seeing the Father. This theological foundation is presented as the antidote to the temptation to add human effort or legalistic observance to the finished work of Christ.

In application, the sermon addresses the modern pluralistic culture that denies the existence of absolute truth. It asserts that Christ is the only way and the culmination of all truth. Believers are encouraged to rest in the sufficiency of Christ, recognizing that God has not withheld any necessary revelation. The call is to remain in Christ, viewing all of Scripture through the lens of His person and work, rather than seeking additional or alternative sources of spiritual authority.
